commit_message:
curl: implement non-blocking STDIN read on Windows

Implements a seperate read thread for STDIN on Windows when curl is run
with -T/--upload-file .

This uses a similar technique to the nmap/ncat project, spawning a
seperate thread which creates a loop-back bound socket, sending STDIN
into this socket, and reading from the other end of said TCP socket in a
non-blocking way in the rest of curl.

Fixes #17451
Closes #17572

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference via strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") when uploadfile is NULL
findings.message: The added non-blocking STDIN read logic in tool_read_cb() checks whether the current transfer uses `-T .` by calling `strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".")` without first verifying that `per->uploadfile` is non-NULL. For transfers that read client input (the read callback) but were not configured with an upload file (`per->uploadfile == NULL`, e.g. plain data-reading operations that still invoke this callback), this call dereferences a NULL pointer inside strcmp(), causing a segmentation fault. The previous code path unconditionally called read() and never referenced per->uploadfile, so this new check introduced a case where the field could be NULL at the point of comparison.
findings.suggestion: Guard the strcmp call with a NULL check on per->uploadfile before comparing it, e.g. `if(per->uploadfile && !strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") && per->infd > 0)`.

ground_truth.root_cause: Missing NULL check before calling strcmp() on a pointer (per->uploadfile) that is not guaranteed to be non-NULL in all code paths that reach tool_read_cb().
